 †*203. SHRI MUKHTA R ABBAS NAQVI: Will the Minister of 
SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether certain Wakf Boards have claimed their rights on certain

As per Education For All (EFA) Global Monitoring Report 2005, the 
literacy rates of some development countries like Sri Lanka and Maldives 
are higher than India whereas literacy rates of other countries like Pakistan, 
Nepal, Bangladesh are much lower than that of India. 
The Universalisation of Elementary Education and eradication of 
adult illiteracy form the two-pronged strategy for improving the literacy 
rate of the country. Sarva Shiksh a Abhiyan (SSA) is a comprehensive 
programme for universalizing quality Elementary Education by 2010. 
The National Literacy Mission (NLM) is entrusted with the target of 
achieving a sustainable level of 75% literacy by 2007. The thrust areas of 
NLM are improving female literacy in low female literacy areas, organizing 
projects for residual illiteracy in districts, which have substantial number 
of illiterates, setting up of continuing education centres for providing 
opportunities for life-long learning to the neo-literates and imparting 
vocational training to neo-literates through Jan Shikshan Sansthans. 
Special programmes for Residual Illiteracy have been taken up in the low 
female literacy districts of Uttar Prad esh, Bihar, Orissa and Jharkhand. In 
addition, the launching of a special literacy drive for eradication of residual 
illiteracy in the 150 districts, which have the lowest literacy rates, has 
been approved. 
The Government has also launched two programmes for education 
of girls at elementary level — the National Programme for Education of 
Girls at the Elementary Level (NPEGEL) and the Kasturba Gandhi Balika 
Vidyalaya (KGBV).

1438. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of 
HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government extend financial assistance to the States 
for spreading computer education in schools; 
84 

[8 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the details thereof with the financial assistance released 
during the last five years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(c) whether on account of inordinate delay in releasing the funds 
under the scheme to the States, the computer education in schools is 
interrupted; 
(d) if so, the details of the outstanding amount under the scheme, 
State-wise; and

uninterrupted progress of computer education in schools in all the States, 
with special reference to Karnataka?

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a)

and Communication Technology (ICT) @ Schools in December, 2004 by 
merging the revised Computer Literacy and Studies in Schools (CLASS) 
Scheme and the Educational Technology (ET) Scheme. Under the scheme 
financial assistance is provided to th e States/UTs in the ratio of 75:25 & 
90:10 as Central Government Share for general category States and special 
category States respectively, for imparting computer education in 
Government and Government aided Secondary and Senior Secondary 
Schools based on the Computer Edu cation Plans (CEPs) received from 
the States/UTs. 
The financial assistance released during the last five years for 
Computer Education is given in the Statement (See below). 
CEPs received from the States of Jammu & Kashmir, Goa, Nagaland, 
Karnataka, Sikkim, Bihar and Rajasthan and UT Administration of Daman 
& Diu were placed before the Project  Monitoring & Ev aluation Group for 
consideration. It has been decided to  release financial assistance to these 
States/UT based on the bu dgetary provisions made by them in their State 
budget. Accordingly, it has been decided to release an amount of 
Rs. 2400.00 Lakhs to the State of Karnataka, provided the State 
Government makes the necessary provision of State and Central share in 
their budget at the time of supplementary grants.

assistance to voluntary organizations 
(a) It should be registered under an appropriate Act or be a regularly 
constituted branch of a registered welfare organization (mere 
affiliation to a registered body will not suffice for this purpose). 
(b) Office bearers of the institution should not be related to each 
other.

registration in order to be eligible for grants from the Board under 
any scheme, except in the scheme of Family Counselling 
Centres where completion of 3 years after registration is required.

those institutions which provide specialized services where these 
are not available; and (iii) in case where the need for starting an 
altogether new service is rec ognized. This re quirement does 
not apply to branches which have been started by well 
established national/State level organizations in remote and 
needy areas. 
(d) It should have a properly constituted Managing Committee with 
its powers, duties and responsibility clearly defined and laid 
down in a written constitution. 
(e) It should have facilities, resour ces, personnel, managerial skill 
and experience to initiate the activity for which the grant is 
required.

position to raise such additional funds, as may be required, to

As per the mandate of the National Policy on Education (NPE)

(d) The salient features of the NCF 2005 are: 
(I) It has based on the following four guiding principles:— 
(i) Connecting knowledge of life outside the school, 
(ii) Ensuring that learning shifts away from rote methods, 
(iii) Enriching the curriculum so that it goes beyond textbooks, 
(iv) Making examinations more flexible. 
(II)The NCF also focuses on the child as an active learner, thus 
giving primacy to the children's experiences, their voices and their 
participation. It views children as active participants in the construction of 
knowledge, and states that schools should recognize the innate ability 
and creativity of each child to construct his/her own knowledge. 
(III) It recommends the softening of su bject boundaries so that children 
can get a taste of integrated knowledge and joy of understanding. 
(IV) It reaffirms faith in panchayati raj institutions to enable people 
to think, decide and act in their collective interest, to provide greater 
participation of people in development.

data on crimes against women compiled by the National Crime Records 
Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs 7,11,778 cases of atrocities on women 
have been reported from various States during 2000 to 2004 for which 
data is available. 
(c) The Government has initiated action in the following areas to 
prevent sexual harassment at workplace as well as other crimes being 
committed against women:— 
• The Government has been propagating the guidelines laid down 
by the Supreme Court in its judgement dated 13.8.1997 in the 
Vishaka case for their strict observation in all workplaces, 
including the direction for setting up of complaints committees 
to deal with complaints of sexual harassment. 
144 

[8 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
• The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 have been 
amended to make sexual harassment a prohibited conduct in 
accordance with the Supreme Court's guidelines. 
• Amendments have also been made in the Industrial Employment 
(Standing Orders) Rules in pursuance of the guidelines. 
• Setting up of helplines for women in distress. 
• Support services to victims of violence through schemes such 
as Short Stay Homes and Swadhar under which shelter, 
maintenance, counselling, capacity building, occupational 
training, medical aid and other services are provided. 
• Grant-in-aid schemes providi ng assistance for rescue and 
rehabilitation of trafficked victims as well as prevention through 
special schemes in source areas of trafficking. 
• Redressal of grievances through interventions of National and 
State Commissions for Women. 
• Organizing Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Camps. 
• Implementation of schemes for (i) awareness generation and 
advocacy and (ii) economic em powerment of women through 
the programmes of Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, Swashakti Project, 
Swayamsidha Project, Swawlamb an Programme and Support 
to Training and Employment Programme (STEP). 
• Periodic review of laws with a view to remove provisions which 
may be discriminatory to women and to enhance punishments 
for crime against women as well as enactment of new laws. 
• Sensitization of judiciary and police and civil administration on 
gender issues. 
• Follow up of reports of cases of atrocities against women 
received from various sources, including NCW, with concerned 
authorities in the Central and the State Governments. 
'Public order' and 'Police' are State subjects as per the Seventh 
Schedule, to the Constitution of India and as such registration, investigation, 
detection and prevention of crime are primarily the responsibility of the

the State Governments, from time to time, to give more focused attention 
to improving the administration of criminal justice system and to take 
such measures as are necessary for the prevention of crime against women 
and other vulnerable sections of society. The measures suggested 
include:—

protecting the women; 
• Vigorously enfore the existing legislation relating to dowry 
violence; 
• Set up women police cells in police stations and exclusive women 
police stations;

• Take measures to eliminate tra fficking in women. States have 
also been advised to constitute  State Advisory Committees to

• Train police personnel in special laws dealing with atrocities

The Copyright Act, 1957, which falls under the purview of the Ministry

authorities of the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

Statement 
An extract of Conference of Law Ministers and Law Secretaries-2005 
Shimla Resolution 
I. Review of the working of Legal Aid System so as to 
strengthen and improve the provisions of the Legal 
Services Authorities Act, 1987: 
Composition of various Legal Services Authorities and 
Committees: 
(i) The Law Ministers were of the general view that the 
composition of various Legal Services Authorities and 
Committees should be broad-based by including therein the 
representatives of the Bar, retired Judges who have 
distinguished themselves in the field of legal aid work and the 
representatives of nodal departments of the Central/State 
Governments/UT Administrations which are concerned with 
issues relating to social welfare, gender justice, etc.

project/mission for legal aid is launched by a Legal Services 
Authority, it should be brought to the notice of the appropriate 
Government in advance, so as to ensure that it does not suffer 
for want of funds at a later stage.

view our limited judi cial manpower, Secretaries of the Legal 
Services Authorities should not only be appointed from 
amongst serving cadre of the Judi cial Services but also from 
sensitised persons. 
(iv) The Law Ministers were of the further view that expenditures 
on tours and conferences and on functions incurred by the 
Legal Services Authorities should not be more than the real 
legal aid to the poor. 
Effective Implementation of the provisions of Chapter VIA of

(v) The Law Ministers were of the view that the constitution of 
separate Lok Adalats for Government Departments and Public 
Sector Undertakings would provide forums for settlement of 
disputes at a minimal cost and with utmost expediency. They 
also recalled the Resolution adopt ed at the First Annual Meet

Government, State Governments and Public Sector 
Undertakings should examine the feasibility of establishing 
separate Lok Adalats for different departments. The Law 
Ministers further recalled that  the Union Law Secretary as

and Public Sector Undertakin gs. The Law Ministers called 
upon the State Governments/U.T. Administrations to set up 
separate Lok Adalats as established by the Central 
Government. 
Lok Adalats under Chapter Vl-A 
(vi) The Law Ministers took note of  the fact that only the States of 
Haryana, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and the U.T. of Chandigarh 
have constituted permanet Lok Adalats for public utility 
services under the provisions of  the new Chapter Vl-A of the 
Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. The Law Ministers also 
177 

RAJYA SABHA [8 August, 2005] 
took note of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 
Writ Petition (Civil) No. 543/2002 in the matter of S.N. Pandey 
Vs. Union of India & Anr. where, while upholding the 
constitutional validity of the provisions of Chapter VIA, it was 
held that this mechanism is undis putedly a fast means of 
dispensation of justice. They took note of the expression of 
hope by the Apex Court that  these Permanent Lok Adalats 
would be set up at the earliest. The Law Ministers, accordingly, 
recommended that all State Governments and UT 
Administrations may consider constituting Permanent Lok 
Adalats under Chapter VIA as early as possible. The Law 
Ministers further recommended that Governments may 
consider inclusion of more public utility services by issuing 
necessary notifications under Section 22A, in addition to the

Criteria for provision of legal aid:

categories of persons entitled to get legal aid under the 1987

like Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal  Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Goa, 
Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Ka rnataka, Maharashtra, Orissa 
and West Bengal and U.Ts. of Chandigarh and Delhi have raised

(ix) The Law Ministers took note of the fact that not maintaining a

emphasized the need for maintaining an approved panel of

Committee, particularly at Distri ct and Taluk levels wherever it 
is not there. 
(x) The Law Ministers also took note of the fact that advocates 
are generally reluctant to take up legal-aid work and that the 
low fee-structure for legal aid advocates in several States, 
makes legal aid workless attractive to them. The Law Ministers 
emphasized the need for prescrib ing a reasonable fee structure

(xi) The Law Ministers considered that adequate representation of 
the advocates belonging to the weaker sections of the society, 
such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Backward 
Classes and Women in the panel of Legal Aid Counsels is 
necessary in order to ensure th at the cases of beneficiaries

†1519. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL Will the Minister of LAW

THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R.

(a)to (c) The Election Commission of India has informed that as per the 
provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the 
Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, only Indian citizens are eligible for 
inclusion in the electoral rolls. However, sometimes during intensive 
revision (House to House enumeration) or summary revision (the period

no data of foreign citizens who have got their names registered in electoral 
roll is available with the Commission.  Whenever such cases of wrongful 
inclusion come to the notice of the Electoral Registration authorities, 
immediate action is taken to remove such names from the electoral roll.

concerns of the tribals; and 
198 

[8 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) wheter these tribal people wo uld not be uprooted from their 
traditional vocations under the new trade regime? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI P. R. KYNDIAH): (a) 
and (c)As indicated by the Ministry of Commerce, under the provisions of 
the TRIPS Agreement of WTO, protection is provided to seven categories 
of intellectual property rights, viz., copyrights and related rights, patents, 
geographical indications, trademarks, industrial designs, layout-desings 
of integrated circuits and undisclosed information. In addition, protection 
is also provided to new plant varieties. Works of traditional tribal artisans 
are prior art and their traditional know ledge fall under public domain and 
therefore these do not belong to any of the above seven categories of 
intellectual property rights. As such, at present no protection is available 
to works of traditional tribal artisans as well as their traditional knowledge 
under the TRIPS Agreement of WTO. 
Tribal Co-operative Marketing Development Federation of India 
Limited (TRIFED) is running a Tribes shop for marketing tribal arts and 
crafts for benefit of scheduled tribe artisans. 
NSTFDC provides financial assistance to eligible Scheduled Tribes 
for income generating schemes including schemes of ST artisans, costing 
upto Rs. 10.00 lakh per unit/profit centre through State Channelising 
Agencies nominated by the respective State/UT Government.  
The Department of Culture, also implements a scheme to promote 
and generate' awareness about richness of tribal/rural culture to inculcate 
respect and admiration for the contribu tion of tribal communities to various 
facets of tribal culture, among other measures. 
(b) The National Tribal Policy seeks to address all concerns of the 
scheduled tribe people.

Regularisation of Industrial clusters 
1544. SHRI AMAR SINGH: 
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have authorised the State Government of 
Delhi to take decisions with regard to the regularisation of the industrial 
clusters in the non-confirming areas; 
219 

RAJYA SABHA [8 August, 2005] 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the names of colonies which are proposed to be declared as 
industrial cluster; and 
(d) by when, a decision is likely to be taken? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM 
NABI 
AZAD): (a) and (b) The Central Government has amended Master Plan for 
Delhi-2001 vide notification dated 31.05.2005, incorporating a provision 
to enable redevelopment of non-conforming clusters of industrial 
concentration subject to fulfilment of prescribed norms and parameters. 
The notification provides that Non-conforming clusters of industrial 
concentration of minimum 4 Ha. contiguous area, having more than 70% 
plots within cluster under manufacturing activity/use may be considered 
for redevelopment on the basis of surveys and issue of notification by the 
Industry Department of Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi 
(GNCTD). The redevelopment scheme shall be prepared by the concerned 
land owning Agency/Society (to be formed by the owners) with the approval 
of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD)/Delhi Development Authority 
(DDA), subject to statutory enviro nmental clearance and clearances from 
other competent Agencies based on the prescribed norms/conditions. 
(c) and (d) The task of survey and identification of clusters that fulfil 
the above norms for redevelopment is  entrusted to GNCTD as per the 
notification.

(b) whether her Ministry asked the Registrar General to conduct a

take stock of the slums in their resp ective States. However, the Town and 
Country Planning Organisation (TCPO) conducted a one time study on 
slums in 1995-96 and brought out a report titled "A Compendium on Indian 
Slums-1996". Each year the Planni ng Commission allocates the State- 
wise funds on the pro-rata basis of slum population of the States/UTs, as 
estimated for 2001 in the above compendium. While deciding such 
allocations a minimum amount is reserved for smaller States.

about slum population of the country but only in cities/towns having 50,000

carried out. The Ministry took up the matter with the Registrar General of

(d) With a view to ameliorate the living conditions of the Urban Poor and 
providing employment opportunities to the urban poor, Ministry of Urban 
Employment & Poverty Alleviation is implementing an employment 
oriented urban poverty alleviati on programme named Swarna Jayanti 
Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY), on a ll India basis with effect from 
1.12.1997. The Scheme is funded in proportion of 75:25 between Centre 
and the States. The SJSRY strives to provide gainful employment to the 
urban unemployed or under-employed poor through (i) encouraging the 
setting up of Self-employment ventures by those who have not studied 
beyond 9th standard and (ii) provision of wage employment by utilizing 
their labour for construction of soci ally and economically useful public 
assets. 
Under SJSRY, Central funds are released to the States/UTs for the 
implementation of the Scheme as per the Guidelines of the Scheme. The 
funds are released to the States /UTs on the basis of prescribed

EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTYALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) 
The 
salient features of the National Action Plan for Total Eradication of Manual 
Scavenging by 2007 are:—

Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993" by all the States

prosecuted for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

Adverse effect of TV programmes and media contents on the 
    mental health of the children and adolescents in the country 
SHRI ANAND SHARMA (Himachal Pradesh): Sir, I beg to call the 
attention of the Minister of Info rmation and Broadcasting to the adverse 
effect of TV programmes and media contents on the mental health of the 
children and adolescents in the country. 
279

THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND THE 
MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRI S. JAIP AL REDDY): Sir, the Government 
is seized of the concerns express ed by the hon. members regarding the 
possible adverse effect of unsuitable content in the electronic media on 
the impressionable minds of children and adolescents. 
For the electronic media, the Programme and Advertising Codes 
prescribe strict guidelines that all channels are expected to adhere to. 
These guidelines specifically prohibit  telecast of programmes unsuitable 
for children, at times when they are likely to be viewed by large numbers.  
An Inter-Ministerial Committee examines  cases of violation of the Codes. 
In the recent past, the permission for transmission of one channel was 
suspended for a period of 30 days. In another case, an offending News 
and Current Affairs channel was asked to telecast a warning issued to it 
by the Ministry of l&B for a period of three days. 
[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair] 
In addition to regulating the channels uplinked from India, the 
Government is also for the first time considering the introduction of 
Downlinking Guidelines for regulating channels uplinked from abroad and 
beamed through satellites into India. 
In a series of interactive workshops with producers of content, the 
Ministry has tried to convey to them the wider concerns expressed in 
regard to issues that include an y adverse impact on children and 
adolescents. We are also contem plating the establishment of an 
autonomous mechanisn to continuous ly monitor and regulate content 
broadcast by the electronic media.

briefly, yet emotionally as I am observing an all round decline in morals 
and values of the present day society wh ich I attribute to the genre of the 
present day television serials.

imagination and attenti on of the common man and the household. They 
spend long hours viewing serials, labelled as family drama, shown by 
many television channels.

The statement also refers to cooperation with the U.S. for enhancing 
capabilities of the Indian Armed Forc es. The U.S. is supplying arms and 
ammunition even to Pakistan and helping it in all aspects. Here is a 
press clipping with me. We are witnessing that India is well aware of the
